# T-201 generic assertion effects: import-boundary nominal identity.
# A Go package with exported generics (p) carries an assert-only
# __.LOGOS member (HasAssert records, proven-zero included). Declaration-
# only members must stamp per-Func metadata in place on the canonical
# imported objects: no package clone, no packages[path] replacement. RED
# on the clone fan-out: q decodes first and captures p's placeholder
# nominals, the later direct import of p replaces packages[p] with a
# clone, and r fails with "cannot use q.Take (variable of type
# func(*p.Box[int])) as func(*p.Box[int])" -- identical spellings,
# distinct *types2.Named. GREEN after the in-place repair: p.Box and
# p.New are pointer-identical through both import orders and the build
# succeeds; the metadata still lands (the unsafe and known-zero
# instantiation semantics are pinned by logos_const_interface_generic_assert).
# Case F imports q before p (placeholder-then-clone order); case R
# imports p before q (order independence).

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd f/r
go build -o diamond$GOEXE .
exec ./diamond$GOEXE
! stderr 'cannot use'
cd ../..

cd r2/r
go build -o diamond$GOEXE .
exec ./diamond$GOEXE
! stderr 'cannot use'
cd ../..

-- p/go.mod --
module example.com/p

go 1.27

-- p/p.go --
package p

// Box and New guarantee a verified HasAssert record (proven zero) in
// p's facts member, exercising the declaration-only import path.
type Box[T any] struct{ V T }

func New[T any](v T) Box[T] { return Box[T]{V: v} }

// An own-type-parameter method has a lazy export pseudo-object. It must
// be decoded through Box, never through package Scope.Lookup("Box.Echo").
func (b Box[T]) Echo[U any](v U) U { return v }

type hidden[T any] struct{ V T }

func (h hidden[T]) Get() T { return h.V }

func MakeHidden[T any](v T) hidden[T] { return hidden[T]{V: v} }


-- q/go.mod --
module example.com/q

go 1.27

require example.com/p v0.0.0

replace example.com/p => ../p

-- q/q.go --
package q

import "example.com/p"

var Take func(*p.Box[int])

func ThroughMethod(v int) int { return p.Box[int]{}.Echo[int](v) }

-- f/r/go.mod --
module example.com/fr

go 1.27

require (
	example.com/p v0.0.0
	example.com/q v0.0.0
)

replace example.com/p => ../../p

replace example.com/q => ../../q

-- f/r/main.go --
package main

import (
	"example.com/q"
	"example.com/p"
)

func main() {
	var take func(*p.Box[int]) = q.Take
	b := p.New(1)
	if q.ThroughMethod(b.V) != 1 || p.MakeHidden(b.V).Get() != 1 {
		panic("lazy generic method metadata mismatch")
	}
	if take != nil && b.V != 1 {
		panic("diamond mismatch")
	}
}

-- r2/r/go.mod --
module example.com/r2r

go 1.27

require (
	example.com/p v0.0.0
	example.com/q v0.0.0
)

replace example.com/p => ../../p

replace example.com/q => ../../q

-- r2/r/main.go --
package main

import (
	"example.com/p"
	"example.com/q"
)

func main() {
	var take func(*p.Box[int]) = q.Take
	b := p.New(1)
	if q.ThroughMethod(b.V) != 1 || p.MakeHidden(b.V).Get() != 1 {
		panic("lazy generic method metadata mismatch")
	}
	if take != nil && b.V != 1 {
		panic("diamond mismatch")
	}
}
